scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Pandanallur style developed primarily in the village of Pandanallur within the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu.
Its foundation stems from the Thanjavur Quartet—four brothers who served as court composers in the early 19th century.
Meenakshisundaram Pillai, a descendant of these nattuvanars, shaped the style into its definitive modern form during his lifetime from 1869 to 1964.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Traditionally performed in classical settings, court contexts, and modern proscenium stages, conveying dramatic storytelling through understated abhinaya and abstract rhythmic passages.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced through rigorous adavu techniques emphasizing linear geometry.
Hard floor stamping is replaced by controlled slow movements that maximize the acoustic output of the salangai ankle bells.
Every step is distinctly marked with exactness and accuracy to achieve rhythmic vitality.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Meenakshisundaram Pillai, the Thanjavur Quartet, Kubernath Tanjorkar, T.K. Swaminatha Pillai, Chokkalingam Pillai, Subbaraya Pillai, and notable students including Rukmini Devi, Mrinalini Sarabhai, Alarmel Valli, and Indrani Rehman.
Migrated from the village of Pandanallur to urban centers like Madras and Baroda through disciples and family members who established teaching hubs.
Descended from the Thanjavur Quartet through Kumarasamy Nattuvanar and Meenakshisundaram Pillai, passing through Chokkalingam Pillai and Subbaraya Pillai to modern practitioners.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Pandanallur style (India). Rhythm pattern: abstract adavu choreography. Instruments: salangai. Mood: intensity, understatement. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
